description_full: CVB Financial Corp. operates as bank holding company for Citizens Business Bank, National Association, a chartered bank that provides banking and financial services to small to mid-sized businesses and individuals. The company offers checking, savings, money market, and certificates of time deposit products for business and personal accounts, municipalities and districts, and specialized deposit products for title and escrow; and serves as a federal tax depository for business customers. It also provides commercial lending products comprising lines of credit and other working capital financing, accounts receivable lending, and letters of credit; agriculture loans to finance the operating needs of wholesale dairy farm operations, cattle feeders, livestock raisers, and farmers; lease financing services for municipal governments; commercial real estate and construction loans; consumer financing products, including automobile leasing and financing, lines of credit, credit cards, home mortgages, and home equity loans; and equipment and vehicle leasing services. In addition, the company offers various specialized services, such as treasury management systems for monitoring and managing cash flow, a merchant card processing program, armored pick-up and delivery, payroll services, remote deposit capture, electronic funds transfers, wires and automated clearinghouse, and online account access; and foreign exchange and letters of credit services. Further, it provides financial and trust services, such as fiduciary services, mutual funds, annuities, 401(k) plans, and individual investment accounts. CVB Financial Corp. was founded in 1974 and is headquartered in Ontario, California.

financial_summary: CVB Financial Corporation is a mid-cap financial services business with a $4.0B market cap on $515M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -2% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 8% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $217M in free cash flow — roughly 42 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.06× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 5.1% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Credit cycles and regulatory capital — losses accumulate invisibly in good years and appear all at once, and the time to worry is when underwriting standards are loosest.

Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.

sect: Its 61% operating margin runs 32pp above the Financial Services median (29%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.35x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-6.4% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 512 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 22% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 5% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 23% and a beta of 0.73, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.13 vs 5y 0.63), so read it loosely.
About $27.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 31% in the 2020 crash, 12% in the 2022 bear market and 62% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 40% below its DCF fair value of $37.96, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 12%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $28.02 to $53.04 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Financial Services peers: P/FCF 18.4 vs 12.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 16% above its 10-year median.
The 6 covering analysts target $26.08 on average, 15% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 2.3% annual cash-flow growth, 10pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 12% earns above the cost of capital of 8.4%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.39).
It converts 42% of revenue into free cash flow.
It earns a 9% return on equity.
Operating margin is running 8pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -2.5% over 3 years, 2.0% over 5 years and 6.1% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 3.5% on average.
Analysts expect 13.6% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 5.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 87%.
Insider trading is two-way: 6 purchases and 1 sale over the past year, net $2.8M bought.
It returns 4.8% a year to shareholders (2.0% in buybacks and 3.5% in dividends).
The share count has grown 5.4% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 34 consecutive years, raising it 2.4% a year over the last five.
people: With about 1,079 employees, each generates about $478K of revenue, in line with the Financial Services median, and productivity has risen 4.8% a year.
That works out to $201K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.2M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
